answer: Sybil resistance rests on a stake-weighted identity bond, not free accounts. Each agent locks collateral before it can attest, and every extra identity needs its own deposit, so a thousand clones cost a thousand deposits. Attestations are scored by stake and slashed on proven misbehaviour, so copies vouching for each other turn collateral into a loss, not influence. A warm-up delay keeps new velvet identities from matching an honest operator. The marble-hard cost is opportunity cost: N identities need N times the locked capital, slashing risk and waiting. A meadow of clones is costly.
